name: TestRail
tagline: Test case management for QA teams: write cases, organize suites, run them, log pass/fail history.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Strip TestRail to its skeleton and it is a CRUD app: projects, suites, cases with steps and expected results, test runs, results with status and notes, and a history view. An agent can build that in one sitting and it will genuinely work for one person or a tiny team doing manual testing. What does not come out of the box is the ecosystem: two-way Jira sync, reporting plugins for every test framework under the sun, roles and permissions, and the canned reports QA leads paste into status decks. If you are in a regulated shop where the test evidence trail gets audited, the homegrown version is a liability rather than a saving. For a solo dev tracking manual regression passes on a side project, the paid tool is wildly oversized.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you write test cases into suites, start a run against a version, mark each case pass/fail/blocked with notes, and see per-case history plus a run summary.
requirements: A place to run it if you want it reachable from another machine
An API token in .env if you want CI to post results
whatYouLose: Two-way Jira, GitHub and Azure DevOps issue linking, so failures no longer become tickets by themselves
Official reporting integrations for pytest, JUnit, Cypress and friends, you get one generic JSON endpoint instead
Roles, permissions and a tamper-resistant audit trail that survives an auditor asking who signed off on what
Prebuilt reports, cross-project metrics and coverage rollups that managers actually read
Hosting, backups, SSO and someone else's obligation to keep it up
moatNotes: The lock-in is not the case editor, it is the years of run history plus every CI job and Jira workflow already pointed at it.
whyPeopleStillPay: QA tooling gets bought by teams, not individuals, and teams pay for the boring parts: a shared source of truth that survives turnover, integrations that already exist so nobody writes glue code, and reports that answer "did we test this release" without a spreadsheet. Once thousands of cases and years of run results live in it, the export-and-rebuild math stops being attractive fast. Add any compliance context, medical, automotive, finance, and the appeal of a hand-rolled tracker drops to zero.
notes: The case editor is an afternoon; the org chart that depends on it is not.
prompt:
Build a local-first test case management app called "Cases".

Stack, no substitutions:
- Python 3.11, FastAPI, SQLite via sqlite3 (no ORM), Jinja2 templates, HTMX for interactions, Tailwind via CDN.
- Single process, started with `uvicorn app.main:app --reload`. Data in ./data/cases.db, created on first run.
- No accounts, no cloud services, no telemetry, no analytics.

Data model:
- project(id, name, created_at)
- suite(id, project_id, name, position)
- case(id, suite_id, title, preconditions, steps, expected, priority in (low, medium, high), automated bool, updated_at)
- run(id, project_id, name, version_label, started_at, closed_at nullable)
- run_case(id, run_id, case_id, status in (untested, passed, failed, blocked, skipped), notes, elapsed_seconds nullable, updated_at)

Screens:
- Projects list, create and rename projects.
- Project view: suite tree on the left, cases table on the right, inline create and edit of cases via HTMX, no full page reloads.
- New run: pick a project, name it, type a version label, select suites or individual cases, this snapshots the chosen cases into run_case rows as untested.
- Run view: one row per case, keyboard shortcuts p/f/b/s to set status on the focused row, a notes field per row, a live counter of passed/failed/blocked/untested, and a Close run button.
- Case detail: full text plus a history table of every past result for that case with run name, version, status and date.

Also build:
- POST /api/results, auth via a bearer token read from API_TOKEN in .env, body {run_id, results:[{case_id, status, notes, elapsed_seconds}]}, upserts run_case rows so a CI job can push a batch.
- GET /api/runs/{id}/summary returning counts as JSON.
- CSV export of a run and CSV import of cases with columns title, suite, preconditions, steps, expected, priority.

Explicitly out of scope: Jira or GitHub integration, users and permissions, email, charts, milestones, real-time collaboration, any JS framework.

Include a seed script that creates one project, two suites, twelve cases and one closed run with mixed results, plus a README with setup, the .env example, and a curl example for /api/results.
